title: fix(plugins): reuse a verified native admission instead of re-capturing it on every catalog refresh
body:
Refs #165686

## What Problem This Solves

An idle Windows Gateway can spend roughly 14 minutes admitting a large native plugin, while the catalog worker abandons it at 180 seconds and captures the same package again. Overlapping hardlink companion directories also repeat member verification. Removing that deadline alone leaves permanently blocked admission hanging without a diagnostic.

## User Impact

An unchanged verified native package is admitted once and reused across catalog refreshes. Slow admission can finish while member verification advances. After 180 seconds without progress, the Gateway records a failure naming the plugin and native reference verification stage, clears pending catalog status, and retains available model facts. That inventory does not automatically restart capture. Reload the plugin or restart the Gateway after addressing the cause to retry.

Parent probes, queued requests, and provider discovery remain bounded. No new configuration, environment switches, CLI options, dependencies, schema changes, or migration are required. Existing integrity checks and cleanup custody remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission belongs to the plugin generation; its existing readiness exchange starts the separate provider-discovery deadline only after preparation. Verified package identities and worker generations remain prepared facts. Within a capture, successful member checks are shared across overlapping companion-directory placements; new placements, namespaces, explicit host selection, recovery, and changed or damaged bytes still require their existing checks.

The watchdog is now minimal: the existing native-reference verifier increments one counter after each verified member. The worker forwards it through the existing task message channel, throttled to once per second while a plugin remains active. The parent reuses its one timer as the 180-second idle window. Plugin changes are forwarded immediately for accurate stall attribution, but only an increasing counter renews that window.

Deleted the separate admission-watchdog, progress, and auth modules. Removed the source-file, hashing, namespace, artifact, inspection-worker, compiler-registration, and full-catalog plumbing from the rejected revision. No separate auth-failure handler remains. The existing worker transport gained a one-way notification because its request/reply exchange permits only one outstanding request and its consumption receipt transfers input custody; neither is a progress channel. This addition is net 9 production lines and does not settle tasks or renew deadlines itself.

Two small pieces remain because the stalled regression fails without them: always invoking the existing catalog failure callback also reports a cold catalog failure; an inventory-level terminal decision prevents a later parent-auth failure from recovering the stalled pool. The catalog mismatch error moved into the existing error module, and repeated completion predicates were consolidated to satisfy the existing line caps without suppressions or baseline changes.

This preserves the original admission fix and leaves the diagnostic probe in #166388 unchanged. Thanks to @martinderm for isolating the admission/deadline loop and @swampgorilla for the original report and diagnostics.

## Evidence

Head: `6fa32a3f42878297a733c97587fae2dd91d0bd8d`. This revision uses a plain push; history was not rewritten. Auto-merge remains off. All proof runs locally with isolated state, without an operator Gateway or remote lease.

The Gateway fixture has 33 hardlinked native artifacts in a 56-file dependency and simulates Windows file-symlink denial. Actual native-reference member operations advance between three 120-second clock steps: 360 simulated seconds complete with one worker, one admission, and two catalog executions using the same captured paths. A held provider hook still fails at its separate 180-second discovery deadline.

A member held indefinitely fails by the 181-second observation point with `PreparedModelCatalogAdmissionStalledError`, the plugin ID, and `native reference verification`. The catalog records the failure immediately, clears pending status, and stays current. An explicit refresh returns the same failure; a real concurrent parent-auth hook then fails independently. After two further idle windows there is still only one worker/capture and no admitted result.

With the current stalled fixture and the r1 parent (`35415a3ae8493f8a64d040075d26eb801b01ea0b`), the regression fails at expiry: expected one recorded failure, received zero. Test execution was 3.902 s, file duration 9.79 s, and wrapper wall time 35.50 s. The final parent was restored byte-for-byte before positive proof.

Negative controls for the two retained pieces:

- With the original cold-catalog callback guard, `records a stalled native admission without restarting its Gateway capture` failed at expiry: expected one recorded failure, received zero (file 11.60 s; wrapper 34.58 s).
- Without the terminal inventory decision, that same test failed after the late parent-auth error: the publication was no longer current. The progressing case passed (stalled case 3.457 s; file 11.74 s; wrapper 33.06 s).

The original loop reproduction recorded 2 workers / 2 capture roots / 0 completed admissions before the admission fix, versus 1 / 1 / 1 afterward (6.458 / 3.966 seconds of test execution). These are fixture results, not a Windows speed claim. The overlapping-directory regression requires one realpath call per sentinel instead of two at each capture/host/recovery boundary; incremental preparation requires no new walk, and changed or damaged companions remain rejected.

The three touched suites passed **15 tests on each of three runs** using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.native.integration.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-artifact.native-reference.test.ts src/infra/worker-task-pool.notifications.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Wall times: **67.52 / 63.95 / 46.41 s**. Progressing case: **5.042 / 8.522 / 4.513 s**; stalled case: **4.055 / 5.355 / 3.301 s**. Maximum RSS including compiler preparation: **5.64 / 0.79 / 0.81 GiB**. The notification test proves synchronous messages reach the parent while a real worker is blocked, without settling its task or consuming input.

All **115 importer files passed: 1,845 tests, two existing skips, 18 Vitest shards**. The importer list came from basename searches and the existing worker-runtime barrels; files ran in the wrapper's original order. Total wall time was **1,033.75 s**, including E2E runtime preparation (the main compiler phase alone took 302.5 s). Maximum RSS including that preparation was **10.25 GiB**. Duplicate reporter summaries were counted once. The reverted scope and inspection fixtures passed unchanged.

Full `pnpm build` passed in **309.9 s**, then passed again on the committed head in **179.3 s**, including Plugin SDK export validation and Control UI build budgets. `git diff --check` and targeted lint passed. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 561ffbfac4f888abc1b6b920885bc81d45ce9c1d` passed, including all 27 test type graphs, core lint, line-cap and assertion guards, exports, schema/storage checks, and zero runtime import cycles. The clean-head Codex cold-import profile qualified with no gaps: **175.47 MiB peak RSS / 0.658 s total CPU**. Its first screen correctly rejected the pre-commit build declaration; the head-bound rebuild supplied the matching declaration. This import profile is separate from native-admission proof.

Pre-existing slow proof remained unchanged, per the campaign ruling. No retries, timeout increases, weaker assertions, or new skips were added.

Fresh isolated Codex autoreview through P1 returned **HTTP 401** and produced no verdict. Per the campaign exception, lead review remains pending; auto-merge is off.

Whole-PR production: **+223 / −119, net +104** across 11 files. Tests and test support: **+425 / −8**. Documentation: **+15 / −4**. No tooling delta remains. The simplification commit itself is **+352 / −625** across 28 files.

Known limits: existing best-effort worker-first SQLite receipt publication warns that shared-state admission requires the host broker. Verified in-process reuse is covered; durable reuse across process restarts is not claimed, and the broker guard is unchanged. The reporter's Windows installation was not run. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available for this revision.
